messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] pushed NNMF model example
parts:
On 1/31/13 7:34 PM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
> Seems to me like it should be a truncated normal likelihood for X, but
> maybe not? I don't actually know the model.

Thanks for pointing this out. (I pasted the current
model below so everyone doesn't have to pull the latest code from
the repository to find it.)

Oh, I forgot to put the constraint on X back in.
It is indeed constrained to be positive.

We do need to truncate the normal at T[0,] to
properly normalize because mu is a variable.
I keep forgetting that we need to do this if there
are variables in the distribution expression, as there
are here.

Too bad, because not only can't we vectorize them,
they're intrinsically slower because of the log CDF
eval.

I can put a manual chapter in for matrix factorization,
but I could use some pointers as to what to include.
So I'd like to talk about models like this at the
meeting a bit. I'm also curious about the effect of
switching the normal out for a lognormal, which
wouldn't need to be truncated, but would skew the noise
(which seems like it might be a good thing in this case).

- Bob

P.S. Here's the model inline to make it easier for everyone
else to see what's going on:

data {
int<lower=0> T;
int<lower=0> I;
int<lower=0> K;
matrix[T,I] X;
real<lower=0> sigma[I];
}
transformed data {
real<lower=0> g_bar;
real<lower=0> g_sigma;
vector[T] temp;
for (t in 1:T)
temp[t] <- log(sum(X[t]));
g_bar <- mean(temp);
g_sigma <- sd(temp);
}
parameters {
matrix<lower=0>[T,K] G;
simplex[I] F[K];
}
model {
for (t in 1:T)
G[t] ~ lognormal(g_bar,g_sigma);

for (t in 1:T) {
vector[I] mu;
for (i in 1:I) {
mu[i] <- 0;
for (k in 1:K) {
mu[i] <- mu[i] + G[t,k] * F[k,i];
}
}
X[t] ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}
}



- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] pushed NNMF model example
parts:
> meeting a bit. I'm also curious about the effect of
> switching the normal out for a lognormal, which
> wouldn't need to be truncated, but would skew the noise
> (which seems like it might be a good thing in this case).

You'd have to be careful about how you parameterized it.
X[t] ~ lognormal(mu, sigma);
would be a very, very different model, since it assumes that factors
combine multiplicatively instead of additively. Who knows, that could
be right for some kinds of data! But then it's not really NNMF, it's
more or less just PCA on log-transformed data. You could instead do
X[t] ~ lognormal(log(mu), sigma);
or
X[t] ~ gamma(1/sigma^2, 1/sigma^2 / mu);
I've done lots of work with the latter kind of model, not so much with
the former.

Matt
